evidence: The workbook row explicitly prohibits naming test paths, and frozen quality-checks.md check 5 explicitly includes /tests in the search. The participant-facing task/environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:414 says, 'The runtime launches Node from `/tests`, which is not the application directory.' instruction.md:7 tells the builder to read that note, and environment/Dockerfile:14 copies the note into /instructions. This is the actual verifier directory (tests/Dockerfile:45: WORKDIR /tests), not an ordinary application path. The frozen template's public integration.md:3-14 establishes entry, storage and dependencies without naming a test directory; no frozen skill or current policy exception authorizes this task-specific disclosure. Source audit verified all 71 frozen task/rule file hashes and the current policy hash; all 76 raw evidence index hashes matched. All three public Markdown files were scanned against 144 criterion IDs/descriptions: no ID collisions or verbatim runs of at least 12 whitespace-delimited words were found. The only other vocabulary hit is 'amortized weight' at hireops_rules.md:20, an ordinary compensation concept and not a grading leak. This row is confirmed by source content; no configured judge score, private checker execution, or exploit success is claimed.
counterexample: The client receives a product brief that reveals the verifier's /tests directory through an explicitly required note, directly violating this row even for a correct app. A plausible broken submission could branch on process.cwd() === '/tests' to enable its working behavior only in the disclosed grading environment; that is a threat-model example, not a measured passing exploit. A conforming alternative resolving assets relative to __dirname and honoring DB_PATH works from any working directory, so it needs only the public constraint that cwd may differ from the app directory, not the literal test path. Rejecting the unrelated compensation phrase 'amortized weight' would instead be a false positive, and this review does not do so.
suggested_fix: In the task-specific note, replace the literal /tests disclosure with 'The runtime may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory' while retaining the absolute/module-relative asset and DB_PATH guidance; leave the shared harness unchanged.
